intro: Hobart's fishing charters work the sheltered water south of the city and the River Derwent estuary. Shared boat trips from Margate Marina, about 15 minutes south of the CBD, bottom fish around Blackmans Bay, Bonnet Hill and Opossum Bay for flathead, Australian salmon, squid and wrasse, and suit beginners and families. Private charters can run offshore into Storm Bay waters for southern bluefin tuna and striped trumpeter.

Hobart is also a base for fly fishing. The lower Derwent estuary holds bream, Australian salmon and sea-run brown trout within minutes of the city, and guides collect anglers from Hobart for day trips to the Derwent Valley rivers and the Central Highlands lakes.
hobart.season: Shared inshore trips target flathead, Australian salmon and squid, while offshore private charters chase tuna and striped trumpeter. Striped trumpeter are closed from 1 September to 31 October, and squid in the south-east region (Lemon Rock to Whale Head) from 15 October to 14 November in 2025 and 2026. Sea-run trout in the Derwent are best from July to September.

p: Boat charters mostly fish inshore reefs and bays south of the city, while trout guides work the Derwent estuary and travel inland.
items: Blackmans Bay, Bonnet Hill and Opossum Bay

p: Rod-and-line fishing in Tasmanian marine waters needs no licence, but rock lobster, abalone, scallops, nets and set lines do, and charter clients must hold any licence the activity requires. Anyone 14 or older fishing for trout needs an Inland Fisheries Service angling licence. Check the current NRE Tas rules for bag and size limits.

faq: Can you catch trout in Hobart itself?

Yes. Sea-run brown trout move through the Derwent estuary, with shore spots from the Tasman Bridge up to the Bridgewater Bridge. One Hobart guide finds late afternoon and evening best, ideally with the tide high or starting to fall. The Derwent below New Norfolk Bridge is an inland water open all year, so an IFS angling licence is needed.
Is there a Hobart fishing trip that combines fishing and diving?

Yes. Diver's Fishing Charters Hobart runs a half-day Hook, Dive and Grill trip from Margate Marina where anglers bottom fish while certified divers explore the same reefs, followed by an onboard barbecue.

intro: Pirates Bay at Eaglehawk Neck is the gateway to the Tasman Peninsula's game fishing water, where the state fisheries agency lists bluefin tuna, mako shark and swordfish among the catch. Charter boats launch here and at Port Arthur for southern bluefin, albacore and striped tuna, and bottom fish the deep reefs for striped trumpeter, tiger flathead, jackass morwong and ocean perch.

The peninsula is about 45 minutes' drive from Hobart Airport. On rough days, calmer bay charters fish Frederick Henry Bay from Dodges Ferry for sand flathead, calamari, Australian salmon and whiting, and some boats run reef trips around Maria Island from Dunalley or Orford.
tasman-peninsula.season: Local charters run tuna trips from about March to August. Bottom and reef fishing runs all year, outside the striped trumpeter closure (1 September to 31 October). Yellowtail kingfish and snapper turn up in the bays from November to March.

p: Frederick Henry, Norfolk and Blackman bays are shark refuge areas: no sharks, skates or rays may be taken other than elephantfish. Maori octopus can be caught recreationally in Eaglehawk Bay. Marine rod-and-line fishing needs no licence; check NRE Tas alerts and the current bag limits before you go.

faq: How far is Eaglehawk Neck from Hobart?
About a 45-minute drive from Hobart Airport, on the road to the Port Arthur Historic Site. Dodges Ferry, used for bay charters, is about 15 minutes from the airport.
Can I keep sharks caught around the Tasman Peninsula?
Not in Frederick Henry, Norfolk or Blackman bays, which are shark refuge areas where sharks, skates and rays other than elephantfish cannot be taken. Check NRE Tas rules for other waters.

intro: Tasmania's Central Highlands is a plateau of more than a thousand lakes, lagoons and tarns holding wild brown trout, and it is the heart of the state's fly fishing. Guides base themselves at Miena on yingina / Great Lake, or collect clients from Hobart, and fish by boat or on foot across Great Lake, Arthurs Lake, Penstock and Little Pine lagoons, Lake Crescent and the remote Western Lakes.

Sight fishing is the local speciality: polaroiding cruising fish, casting to tailing trout on flooded margins and fishing mayfly hatches and gum beetle falls. The weather can swing from calm sun to sleet even in summer, so guides plan several options for each day.
central-highlands.season: Most brown trout waters are open from the first Saturday in August to the Sunday nearest 30 April: 1 August 2026 to 2 May 2027. Great Lake is open all year except Canal Bay (28 November 2026 to 28 March 2027 only). Designated rainbow trout waters open 3 October 2026. Guides report dry fly fishing improving as the weather warms through spring and summer.

items: Great Lake (yingina)

p: Anyone 14 or older needs an Inland Fisheries Service angling licence, including guided clients; licences come in 48-hour, 7-day, 28-day, season and five-season versions. Waters flowing into Great Lake, Lake Leake, Arthurs Lake and Dee Lagoon are closed, along with 50 m below where they enter. Trout Weekend runs at the IFS Liawenee Field Station on 10 and 11 October 2026.

faq: Can you fish Great Lake in winter?
Yes. Great Lake is open all year except Canal Bay, which opens only from 28 November 2026 to 28 March 2027. Most other highland waters close in early May.
Do I need an angling licence at Currawong Lakes?
No. An angling licence is not needed at registered private fisheries such as Currawong Lakes, but access fees apply.

intro: Launceston and the Northern Midlands are Tasmania's river country. Guides based in Launceston and at Cressy in the Northern Midlands fish the meadow streams and tailwaters for wild brown and rainbow trout: Brumbys Creek, the South Esk, Macquarie, Meander, North Esk, St Patricks and Mersey rivers, with most water within an hour's drive of accommodation.

Trips are wading or drifting by raft or boat, and many include tuition, so the region suits first-timers as well as experienced dry fly anglers. Longer trips reach the Central Highlands lakes, the Currawong Lakes private fishery, or the Western Lakes wilderness beside the Walls of Jerusalem National Park.
launceston.season: Most rivers are open from 1 August 2026 to 2 May 2027, and the lower sections of Brumbys Creek and the Macquarie, Meander and South Esk rivers stay open until 30 May 2027. One local river guide says dry fly fishing becomes the norm after early October. The kanamaluka / Tamar below the Charles Street and West Tamar Road bridges is open all year.

p: Every angler aged 14 or over needs an Inland Fisheries Service angling licence, and some guides can sell one. Registered private fisheries such as Currawong Lakes don't require a licence but charge access fees. Launceston has direct flights from Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane.

faq: Can I do a half-day fly fishing trip from Launceston?
Yes. Tasmania Fly Fishing runs private half days (8.30am-12.30pm or 1.30-5.30pm) on rivers, streams and small lakes close to Launceston, aimed at beginners and visitors short on time.
Which Launceston-area rivers stay open after the main season closes?
The lower sections of Brumbys Creek and the Macquarie, Meander and South Esk rivers stay open until 30 May 2027, four weeks after most waters close.

p: Tasmania's charter and guide industry splits into salt water in the south-east and east, and trout country inland. Boats work out of Hobart and the Tasman Peninsula, with East Coast charters at St Helens, while professional trout guides operate from Hobart, Miena in the Central Highlands, Launceston and Cressy.
items: Hobart & Storm Bay
Inshore bottom fishing for flathead, salmon and squid, offshore tuna and striped trumpeter, and Derwent estuary fly fishing
Tasman Peninsula
Pirates Bay and Port Arthur for southern bluefin and albacore tuna, deep reef fishing and calmer bay trips
St Helens & the East Coast
Georges Bay and offshore reefs and game fishing; charters run both inside the bay and offshore
Central Highlands
Great Lake, Arthurs Lake, the shallow lagoons and the Western Lakes for wild brown trout on fly
Launceston & the North
Midlands rivers such as Brumbys Creek, the South Esk and Meander for river fly fishing

p: Salt water fishes all year, with tuna off the Tasman Peninsula from about March to August. Striped trumpeter are closed from 1 September to 31 October. Most trout waters open on 1 August 2026 and close on 2 May 2027; Great Lake and several lowland waters stay open all year.

Rod-and-line fishing in marine waters needs no licence; rock lobster, abalone, scallops, nets and set lines do, and charter clients must hold any licence the activity requires. Inland, everyone 14 or older needs an IFS angling licence, guided clients included; short-term 48-hour, 7-day and 28-day licences are available and junior licences (14-17) are free.

faq: Do I need a fishing licence on a Tasmanian charter boat?

Not for rod and line in the sea. NRE Tas says charter clients need the appropriate recreational licence only for licensed activities such as rock lobster, abalone or scallops. Trout fishing in inland waters always needs an Inland Fisheries Service angling licence for anyone 14 or older.
When does the Tasmanian trout season open?

Most waters open on the first Saturday in August (1 August 2026) and close on the Sunday nearest 30 April (2 May 2027). Designated rainbow trout waters run from 3 October 2026 to 30 May 2027, and some waters, including Great Lake, are open all year.
